statement.essentials: The wound is closed in layers, with fine stitches in the skin so the scar is neat.
statement.anatomy: Deep tissue and the skin are closed separately: absorbable stitches under the skin, and fine stitches in the skin itself, finer on the face than in the neck.
statement.clinical: The University of Iowa protocol closes the subcutaneous tissue with 3-0 or 4-0 absorbable sutures (Vicryl or chromic) and the skin with a combination of running and interrupted 5-0 nylon in the neck and 6-0 nylon on the face. A pressure dressing is used until the patient is awake and then removed if a suction drain is used.

limitations: One institution's practice. Suture material, technique and dressing vary between surgeons.
